content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD and Test Infrastructure
a: marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with experience owning CI/CD pipelines and test infrastructure for three product teams. Built Kubernetes-based ephemeral environments, reduced pipeline times and developed monitoring for test reliability. Personal infrastructure projects include Terraform provisioning, GitOps and observability. Seeking a DevOps or platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and infrastructure: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes
Infrastructure as code and GitOps: Terraform, Argo CD, Ansible (basic); personal projects
Cloud and virtual machines: Hetzner VPS; AWS EC2 and S3 basics through personal learning
Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki
Languages and data: Python, Bash, SQL, Java (test code), PostgreSQL
Other: Linux, Git, pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer, Test Infrastructure | Odrava Health Software | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams of approximately 25 developers, covering builds, unit, integration and end-to-end tests, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes through parallel test jobs, dependency caching and changes to end-to-end testing; monthly CI runner costs fell by approximately 30%.
- Built merge-request environments, initially with Docker Compose and later with Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically destroyed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Write Helm charts and work with namespace-level access; the platform team operates the shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests. Built Grafana dashboards from CI results to identify flaky tests; the flaky rate fell from 7% to below 1% as teams fixed the top offenders.
- Wrote Bash and Python tools for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and internal CI documentation used in onboarding.
- Mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects, using manual and automated methods.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium regression suite for the largest client project and configured Jenkins for nightly runs. Previously, a full manual regression took two people three days.
- Rewrote a small portion of API tests in Python as practice.

Customer Support Specialist, 2nd Line | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

PERSONAL PROJECT

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster with applications deployed from Git using Argo CD.
- Used Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik for ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a personal Hetzner VPS with Terraform.

EDUCATION AND CERTIFICATIONS
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | Studying; exam booked for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish: Native | English: C1 | German: A2

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional, metrics-driven CV with clear section headings and a convincing progression from QA automation into CI/CD and test infrastructure. The quantified results are effective: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The document also responsibly distinguishes professional Kubernetes responsibilities from the platform team's cluster ownership and identifies Terraform, AWS, and Ansible exposure as personal or basic experience. The main content weakness is that the CV underuses evidence of communication, stakeholder support, documentation, and technical leadership that exists in the candidate material.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard, ATS-friendly headings, reverse-chronological experience, conventional bullet points, and searchable technology names. The technical skills section includes relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS EC2, S3, Prometheus, Grafana, Linux, and PostgreSQL. ATS readability could be improved slightly by replacing the nonstandard 'a:' contact prefix with explicit labels such as Email, Phone, and GitLab, and by making the CKA status unmistakably 'in progress' rather than presenting it within a certifications heading. The document correctly does not claim Terragrunt, mTLS, production on-call, or production cluster administration, so those keywords should not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a credible foundation for hands-on infrastructure engineering: the candidate owns CI/CD pipelines, builds ephemeral Kubernetes environments, writes Helm charts, uses Terraform in personal infrastructure work, and operates observability tooling in a homelab. It aligns particularly well with Linux, virtual machines, analytical problem-solving, reliability, monitoring, and practical delivery ownership. AWS exposure is present but limited to personal learning, while Terraform is personal/project-based rather than demonstrated as strong production Terraform. The candidate's material does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, broader networking, systems architecture, practical security beyond TLS-related tooling, IoT or remote-device integration, or backend/full-stack development. The role also appears to expect a highly autonomous infrastructure contractor who can shape architecture and lead technical proposals, whereas the CV currently presents a strong QA-to-DevOps transition profile rather than established senior cloud infrastructure experience. Evidence of mentoring, onboarding documentation, and supporting QA/product stakeholders should be made more visible because it is relevant to the role's communication and technical-leadership expectations.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. MINOR ATS FIX — In the contact line beneath the name, replace "a: marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example" with clearly labelled, parseable fields such as "Email: marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | Phone: +48 555 303 303 | GitLab: https://gitlab.com/mkb-example".

2. IMPORTANT ACCURACY/ATS CLARIFICATION — In the Education and Certifications section, change "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | Studying; exam booked for January 2027" to "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — In progress; exam scheduled for January 2027 (not yet certified)". This prevents automated or human screening from interpreting CKA as an already-earned certification.

3. JOB-ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT — In the Professional Experience section under "QA Automation Engineer, Test Infrastructure | Odrava Health Software", add a bullet based on the candidate material: "Wrote the internal 'how our CI works' documentation used for onboarding, helping developers and QA engineers understand pipeline workflows and responsibilities." This makes communication, documentation, and stakeholder enablement visible without overstating formal technical leadership.

4. JOB-ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT — In the same Odrava Health Software subsection, revise the existing merge-request environment bullet to include the documented user impact. For example: "Built merge-request environments ...; QA and product teams use them to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment." This directly demonstrates collaboration with stakeholders and support for teams deploying and operating software.

5. JOB-ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT — In the same Odrava subsection, add the documented mentoring responsibility as a separate final bullet: "Mentored two QA interns in 2023, providing guidance on automation and test-infrastructure practices." This supports the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing others along, while accurately presenting the scope as mentoring rather than formal infrastructure leadership.

6. MINOR STRUCTURE IMPROVEMENT — In the Technical Skills section, separate professional and personal exposure more explicitly within each relevant category. For example, use "Professional: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access)" and "Personal projects: Terraform, Argo CD, Ansible (basic), AWS EC2/S3 basics, Hetzner VPS." This preserves the current truthful distinctions while making the candidate's production scope easier to assess.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible CV with clear progression from QA automation into CI/CD and test infrastructure. The quantified results—pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%—provide convincing evidence of impact. The document is also appropriately transparent about personal versus professional experience and Kubernetes access level. The main content weakness is that the target role is cloud infrastructure/DevOps, while much of the professional experience is still framed around QA and test infrastructure. There is also a duplicated point about the internal CI documentation, which should be consolidated.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, chronological experience, searchable technology names, and ATS-friendly plain text formatting. It should parse reliably and has good keyword coverage for GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitOps, AWS, Linux, Grafana, Prometheus, and PostgreSQL. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to good for junior or mid-level DevOps/platform roles, but lower for this particular contractor role because the CV does not demonstrate several high-priority terms from the advertisement: Terragrunt, systems architecture, networking, mutual TLS, practical security, and cloud production operation. Do not add those terms unless supported by real experience. The skills section could be made more consistent by separating professional experience, personal projects, and proficiency level in a uniform format.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows credible hands-on infrastructure-adjacent work: ownership of CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral environments deployed with Helm to Kubernetes, test infrastructure, observability, Linux, and personal Terraform/GitOps work. It also demonstrates analytical thinking and communication through measurable optimization work, dashboards, onboarding documentation, and mentoring. AWS exposure is present but limited to personal learning and basic EC2/S3 work. The candidate's material does not show strong Terraform and Terragrunt experience, systems architecture ownership, networking or mTLS, practical security work, IoT/remote-device integration, or backend/full-stack development. These are genuine capability gaps for this specific role, not defects that can be fixed by wording. The CV is better aligned with a junior-to-mid DevOps, platform engineering, CI/CD infrastructure, or developer productivity role than with a contractor expected to shape production train-to-cloud architecture independently.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified. The document does not contain apparent unsupported skills or experience when cross-referenced with the original candidate information.

MINOR BUT MEANINGFUL IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the infrastructure scope and evidence more explicit without overstating cloud or production ownership. For example, change the current summary to: "QA automation engineer with experience owning GitLab CI pipelines and test infrastructure for three product teams. Built short-lived merge-request environments with Docker Compose and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster, reduced pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, and developed Grafana-based test reliability monitoring. Personal projects include Terraform provisioning, GitOps, and observability." This leads with the most relevant transferable experience and preserves the professional/personal distinction.
2. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, combine the two bullets about internal CI documentation into one bullet. Retain: "Wrote the internal 'how our CI works' documentation used in onboarding, helping developers and QA engineers understand pipeline workflows and responsibilities." Remove the duplicate version.
3. In the Odrava Health Software section, make the stakeholder impact of the ephemeral environments more prominent by retaining the supported details in one concise bullet: "Built merge-request environments containing the application, PostgreSQL, and seeded data; QA and product teams used them to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment." This better supports the requirement for communication and bringing stakeholders along.
4. In the Technical Skills section, standardize the labels so ATS and human reviewers can distinguish demonstrated professional experience from personal exposure. For example, use separate lines titled "Professional infrastructure experience," "Personal projects and learning," "Monitoring and observability," and "Development and testing." Keep the existing qualifiers such as "namespace-level access," "basic," and "personal projects" rather than implying production cloud or cluster administration.
5. In the Personal Project section, include the supported networking and security-adjacent technologies already present in the candidate material by revising the bullet to: "Used Prometheus, Grafana, and Loki for monitoring; Traefik for ingress; and cert-manager for TLS." This improves keyword coverage for observability, ingress, and TLS without claiming mTLS or broader security experience.
6. In the Technical Skills section, change "AWS EC2 and S3 basics" to "AWS: EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning)" and retain "Hetzner VPS" as personal experience. This makes the limited nature of the cloud exposure immediately clear while preserving relevant AWS keywords.
